The '''KNVB Beker''' ({{IPA|nl|ˌkaːʔɛɱveːˈbeː ˈbeːkər|pron}}; {{langx|en|'''KNVB Cup'''}}), branded as the '''Eurojackpot KNVB Beker''' for sponsorship reasons, is a competition in the [[Netherlands]] organised by the [[Royal Dutch Football Association]] (KNVB) since 1898.<ref>{{Cite web |title=TOTO KNVB Beker |url=https://www.knvb.nl/competities/toto-knvb-beker |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180615190618/https://www.knvb.nl/competities/toto-knvb-beker |archive-date=15 June 2018 |access-date=27 July 2022 |website=KNVB}}</ref> It was based on the format of the English [[FA Cup]]. Outside the Netherlands, it is often referred to as the '''Dutch Cup'''. The tournament consists of all teams from the top four tiers of Dutch league football ([[Eredivisie]], [[Eerste Divisie]], [[Tweede Divisie]] and [[Derde Divisie]]), as well as the 24 semi-finalists (or replacements) of the six [[KNVB District Cup]]s. The finals of the tournament traditionally takes place in [[Feijenoord Stadion|De Kuip]], and has been held there every season since the 1989 final. The winners of the cup compete against the winners of the Eredivisie for the [[Johan Cruyff Shield]], (equivalent to a super cup) which acts as the curtain raiser for the following season.

==History==
===Early history===
The first attempt to hold a knock-out competition open to all clubs in the Netherlands was made in 1894, with the winners receiving a trophy offered by H.M.C. Holdert, former president of [[VVA/Spartaan|V.V.A. (Amsterdam)]].<ref name=RSSSF>{{cite web |url=https://www.rsssf.org/tablesn/ned1894.html#beeld |title=Netherlands 1893/94 - Holdert-beeld |publisher=[[RSSSF]] |date=30 August 2024 |access-date=1 November 2024 }}</ref> Seven teams entered and the first ever cup match in the Netherlands was thus held on 11 February, between [[HFC Haarlem|Haarlem]] and [[Koninklijke HFC|HFC]], ending in a 3–1 win to the latter.<ref name=RSSSF/> However, no other match was played due to the withdraws of several teams, and the lack of interest shown by the clubs caused Holdert to withdraw his trophy, so the final between HFC and [[AVV RAP|R.A.P.]] was canceled,<ref name=RSSSF/> but four years later, in January 1898, Holdert offered another cup, to be contested just like the English [[FA Cup]], and thus the KNVB Cup was conceived during a board meeting of the Dutch Football Association, in [[The Hague]], on 19 January 1898.<ref name=RSSSF98>{{cite web |url=https://www.rsssf.org/tablesn/ned1898.html#beker |title=Netherlands 1897/98 - Holdert-beeld |publisher=[[RSSSF]] |date=30 December 2023 |access-date=1 November 2024 }}</ref> Initially, it was decided to stage a competition for this new trophy already in the ongoing 1897–98 season, but the board had to cancel it after a prolonged stretch of bad weather in the first weeks of February had led to numerous match postponements in the western leagues.<ref name=RSSSF98/>

The tournament finally began the following season, [[1898–99 KNVB Cup|1898–99]]. The first [[1899 KNVB Cup final|final]] was played on 9 May 1899 between [[AVV RAP|RAP Amsterdam]] and [[HVV Den Haag]], and ended in a 1–0 victory for the former thanks to a goal from [[Jan Hisgen]] in [[Overtime (sports)#Association football|extra-time]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=23 November 2013 |title=Nederlandse voetbalbeker 1898-99 |trans-title=Dutch Football Cup 1898-99 |url=https://www.voetbalkroniek.nl/2013/11/nederlandse-voetbalbeker-1898-99.html |access-date=1 November 2024 |website=Voetbalkroniek |language=nl}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=31 January 2018 |title=1899: R.A.P. wint den holdertbeker |trans-title=1899: R.A.P. wins the holding cup |url=https://www.totoknvbbeker.nl/100-finales/1899-r.a.p.-wint-den-holdertbeker |access-date=1 November 2024 |website=TOTO KNVB Beker |language=nl}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=https://sportgeschiedenis.nl/sporten/voetbal/ook-in-de-eerste-bekerfinale-stond-een-ploeg-uit-amsterdam/ |title=Ook in de eerste bekerfinale stond een ploeg uit Amsterdam |trans-title=A team from Amsterdam also appeared in the first cup final |language=nl |website=sportgeschiedenis.nl |date=16 April 2022 |access-date=1 November 2024 }}</ref>

In 1946, the trophy was changed to one made out of silver, which was extremely rare in the immediate aftermath of [[World War II]]. That trophy remains in use today.

===Recent history===
In 2018, a trophy colored in gold was commissioned to commemorate the 100th edition of the tournament.<ref name="GOLD">{{cite web |date=12 January 2018 |title=TOTO nieuwe naamgever KNVB Beker en Gouden Trofee |trans-title=TOTO new namesake KNVB Cup and Golden Trophy |url=https://www.knvb.nl/nieuws/betaald-voetbal/toto-knvb-beker/45535/toto-nieuwe-naamgever-knvb-beker-en-gouden-trofee |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221102171510/https://www.knvb.nl/nieuws/betaald-voetbal/toto-knvb-beker/45535/toto-nieuwe-naamgever-knvb-beker-en-gouden-trofee |archive-date=2 November 2022 |accessdate=27 July 2022 |website=KNVB |language=nl}}</ref>

===Name changes===
Like many national cup competitions, the name of the tournament has changed with sponsorship. From 1995, the competition went from being the '''KNVB Beker''' to being known as the '''Amstel Cup''' after the then sponsor [[Amstel Brewery|Amstel]]. On 16 August 2005, the name was changed to the '''Gatorade Cup''' after the drinks company [[Gatorade]]. In 2006, the name returned to being the '''KNVB Beker''' with Gatorade remaining as the principal sponsor.

On 12 January 2018, it was announced that TOTO would become the title sponsor of the KNVB Cup through the 2021–22 season, immediately rebranding the competition as the '''TOTO KNVB Beker'''.<ref name=GOLD/>

On 10 June 2025, a new landmark sponsorship agreement was announced with EUROJACKPOT, marking a change in title sponsorship for the first time since 2018. Under the five-year deal, running through the 2029–30 season, the competition was renamed the '''Eurojackpot KNVB Beker'''.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Eurojackpot nieuwe naamgevend hoofdsponsor van KNVB Beker en Vrouwen Eredivisie |url=https://www.eurojackpotknvbbeker.nl/nieuws/toto-knvb-beker/eurojackpot-nieuwe-naamgevend-hoofdsponsor-van-knvb-beker-en-vrouwen |access-date=2026-04-29 |website=www.eurojackpotknvbbeker.nl}}</ref>

===European competition===
Up until 1998, the winner of the cup entered into the [[UEFA Cup Winners' Cup]], but with the abandonment of that tournament, the winner now goes into the [[UEFA Europa League]]. If the winning team has finished in the top two of the [[Eredivisie]] and thus gained entry into the [[UEFA Champions League]], the berth will be redistributed to that season's Eredivisie.

In 1998, both KNVB Cup finalists, [[AFC Ajax|Ajax]] and [[PSV Eindhoven|PSV]], gained entry in the Champions League, so a third-place play-off was played between the beaten semi-finalists, [[SC Heerenveen]] and [[FC Twente]], to determine who would take the Cup Winners' Cup place.

==Media coverage==
The broadcast rights are included in the [[KNVB]] broadcast rights package, which also includes the [[Johan Cruyff Shield]].

The KNVB Cup is currently broadcast live by the [[ESPN (Netherlands)|ESPN]] channels.
